# Parity Between Occurrences

This notebook makes concrete the automaton of the chapter's *parity* example (adapted from Wolfgang Thomas). Over $\Sigma=\{a,b,c\}$ we recognise:

> *Between any two consecutive occurrences of $a$, there is an **even** number of $b$ and $c$ symbols combined.*

For instance $a\,b\,c\,a$ is accepted (two symbols between the $a$'s), while $a\,b\,b\,b\,a$ is rejected (three). Words with **no** $a$, or only **one** $a$, satisfy the condition *vacuously*.

The point of the example is that **each state carries a precise invariant**:

- $q_0$ — before the first $a$ (or no $a$ at all). **Accepting.**
- $q_1$ — an *even* number of $b/c$ since the last $a$ (zero counts as even). **Accepting.**
- $q_2$ — an *odd* number of $b/c$ since the last $a$. **Non-accepting.**

Reading $a$ from $q_2$ would close an **odd** gap and violate the property: that transition is simply **undefined**, so the run dies. Notice $q_2$ need not be accepting — see the widget's note below.

```{=html}
<div class="sc-lab" id="nb15">

        <text x="50" y="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b,c</text>
        <!-- q0 -> q1 a -->
        <path d="M 74 70 L 126 70" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#nb15-arr)"/>
        <text x="100" y="60" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">a</text>
        <!-- q1 loop a -->
        <path d="M 150 52 C 132 12, 188 12, 170 52" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb15-arr)"/>
        <text x="160" y="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">a</text>

        <path d="M 184 60 C 210 44, 236 44, 262 60" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb15-arr)"/>
        <text x="223" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b,c</text>
        <!-- q2 -> q1 b,c -->
        <path d="M 262 82 C 236 98, 210 98, 184 82" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb15-arr)"/>
        <text x="223" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b,c</text>

        <g transform="translate(60,70)"><circle r="24" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle r="19" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">q&#8320;</text></g>
        <g transform="translate(160,70)"><circle r="24" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle r="19" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">q&#8321;</text></g>
        <g transform="translate(273,70)"><circle r="19" fill="#e8e8f0" stroke="#999" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">q&#8322;</text></g>

      <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--sc-label);margin:10px 0 0;">
        <strong>Why q&#8322; is not accepting:</strong> if no further $a$ ever comes, the
        run bounces $q_1\leftrightarrow q_2$ forever and visits $q_1\in F$
        infinitely often anyway — $q_1$ alone witnesses acceptance. If an $a$
        does come while in $q_2$, the transition is undefined and the run
        dies. Either way $q_2$ carries no acceptance information.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="sc-panel">
      <h4>Run trace &rho; (stem + 3 periods)</h4>
      <div class="run-strip" id="nb15-strip"></div>
      <div id="nb15-verdict"></div>
    </div>

<script>
(function(){
  const delta = {
    q0: {a:'q1', b:'q0', c:'q0'},
    q1: {a:'q1', b:'q2', c:'q2'},
    q2: {b:'q1', c:'q1'}            // q2 on 'a' -> undefined (dead)
  };
  const F = new Set(['q0','q1']);
  const PRESETS = [
    {u:'', v:'a b c'}, {u:'', v:'a b b c'}, {u:'a', v:'b c'},
    {u:'', v:'a b'}, {u:'', v:'b c'}
  ];
  const parse = s => s.trim().split(/[\s,]+/).filter(x=>x.length);

  function run(){
    const u = parse(document.getElementById('nb15-u').value);
    const v = parse(document.getElementById('nb15-v').value);
    const strip = document.getElementById('nb15-strip');
    const verdict = document.getElementById('nb15-verdict');
    strip.innerHTML=''; verdict.innerHTML='';
    if(v.length===0){ verdict.innerHTML="<div class='verdict-box verdict-fail'>Period cannot be empty.</div>"; return; }

    const maxSteps = u.length + v.length*3;
    let state='q0'; addStep(strip,'',state,false);
    const tail=new Set(); let dead=false; let deadSym='';
    for(let i=0;i<maxSteps;i++){
      const sym = i<u.length ? u[i] : v[(i-u.length)%v.length];
      if(!['a','b','c'].includes(sym)){ verdict.innerHTML=`<div class='verdict-box verdict-fail'>Unknown symbol "${sym}". Alphabet is {a,b,c}.</div>`; return; }
      const nxt = delta[state][sym];
      if(nxt===undefined){ addStep(strip,sym,state,true); dead=true; deadSym=sym; break; }
      state=nxt; addStep(strip,sym,state,false);
      if(i>=u.length) tail.add(state);
    }
    if(dead){
      verdict.innerHTML=`<div class='verdict-box verdict-fail'><strong>Rejected.</strong> Reading <code>${deadSym}</code> from ${sub('q2')} closes an <em>odd</em> block — the transition is undefined, so the run dies. No infinite run exists.</div>`;
      return;
    }
    const inF=[...tail].filter(q=>F.has(q));
    let html=`<div class="verdict-box ${inF.length?'verdict-pass':'verdict-fail'}">`;
    html+=`In(&rho;) = { ${[...tail].sort().map(sub).join(', ')} }<br>`;
    html+=`In(&rho;) &cap; F = { ${inF.sort().map(sub).join(', ')} }<br><br>`;
    html+= inF.length ? `&rarr; <strong>Accepted.</strong> ${sub(inF[0])} is visited infinitely often: every <em>b/c</em> block between consecutive <em>a</em>'s is even (or there is at most one <em>a</em>).` : `&rarr; <strong>Rejected.</strong>`;
    html+=`</div>`;
    verdict.innerHTML=html;
  }
  function addStep(c,sym,state,dead){
    const box=document.createElement('div'); box.className='run-step';
    const s=document.createElement('div'); s.className='run-sym'; s.innerHTML=sym===''?'&nbsp;':sym;
    const st=document.createElement('div'); st.className='run-state'+(dead?' dead':(F.has(state)?' accept':''));
    st.innerHTML = dead ? '&#10007;' : subPlain(state);
    box.appendChild(s); box.appendChild(st); c.appendChild(box);
  }
  const sub = q => 'q<sub>'+q[1]+'</sub>';
  const subPlain = q => 'q'+q[1];

  function loadPreset(){
    const p=PRESETS[+document.getElementById('nb15-preset').value];
    document.getElementById('nb15-u').value=p.u;
    document.getElementById('nb15-v').value=p.v;
    run();
  }
  document.getElementById('nb15-preset').addEventListener('change',loadPreset);
  document.getElementById('nb15-run').addEventListener('click',run);
  ['nb15-u','nb15-v'].forEach(id=>document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('keyup',e=>{if(e.key==='Enter')run();}));
  loadPreset();
})();
</script>
```

---

Related: **[Notebook 12 — Büchi Automaton Runner](12-buchi-runner.qmd)** runs the simpler "infinitely many saves" automaton; here the state set encodes a genuine *counting* invariant (parity), which is why the automaton stays deterministic with only three states.
